decision.architecture_verdict: NO CANON CHANGE / SHADOW RESEARCH ONLY
decision.reason: The dominant 2026-09-28 losses localize primarily to Common ordered-pair/head×P2 transport, pair-conditioned third, exact orientation, capital topology, FINAL temporal freeze and rendered closure correctness. The Funabashi-specific mechanisms proposed for research—leadership acquisition/survival, pressure/friction, tracking cost, stage transition and same-day track-state interpretation—already exist in v2.1. One meeting-day does not justify duplicative v2.2 rules.

existing_v2_1_coverage.implication: Do not add duplicate Leadership Acquisition, Survival, Front Friction, Tracking Cost or Heavy-track Stage-transition clauses merely to explain 2026-09-28.

common_correctness_handoff.architecture_rule: REUSE EXISTING VALIDATION AND TRANSPORT STAGES; DO NOT ADD A NEW VENUE VALIDATOR
acceptance_requirements: Frozen semantic existence, MEC-selected coverage unit, canonical ticket and rendered FINAL ticket array must be distinguishable.
If a unit was selected by MEC/decision policy but absent from canonical/rendered ticket, fail closed as ticket-transport correctness failure.
If a semantic unit existed but MEC did not select it, classify as MEC/selection decision rather than transport failure.
If MEC selected and canonical ticket contains it but rendered FINAL omits or mutates it, classify as rendered round-trip failure.
No pre-result immutable FINAL => no Formal/Frozen PFS authority.
Correctness repair must not create extra purchases or change Prediction policy by itself.

hypotheses.name: Front Friction / Tracking Cost
hypotheses.preregistered_question: Under high front-demand/friction states, does low-cost tracking/progression evidence improve W/P2 ordering versus absolute early position alone?
